title: Odysseus notes - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen excerpts Georgi Gospodinov's novel Time Shelter, whose premise is that refuges recreating past decades are built for Alzheimer's patients and then people from the present start wanting to live in them. The quoted passage recasts Odysseus in old age as literally becoming 'Nobody' — the alias he once used on the Cyclops — found collapsed a hundred yards from a home he no longer recognizes.

insights.claim: Georgi Gospodinov's novel Time Shelter is built on the premise that refuges are constructed for Alzheimer's patients that reproduce life from past decades, for instance the 1960s.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A fictional frame for the real market in immersive period environments and memory-care design — reminiscence therapy is already a commercial category.
insights.locator: The novel is Time Shelter, and the premise

insights.claim: In Time Shelter the demand for past-decade refuges does not stay confined to the memory-impaired — people from the present start wanting to live in them too.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: The generalizable point Cowen is flagging: appetite for retreat into curated pasts scales beyond its clinical justification, a demand pattern visible in retro media, analog devices and heritage consumption.
insights.quote: But then people from the present start wanting to live in them.

insights.claim: The excerpted 'shortest novel about Odysseus' has the aged hero secretly leave home to revisit the places, women and wonders he once encountered, because he is beginning to transform into the Nobody — the name he had cleverly used when introducing himself to the Cyclops.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A compact image of how cognitive decline dissolves the reputational identity that careers and legacies are built on — relevant to succession and founder-dependence risk.
insights.quote: he has begun to transform into the Nobody, the name he had once cleverly used when introducing himself to the Cyclops
insights.locator: The Shortest Novel About Odysseus After His Return Home

insights.claim: In the passage, Telemachus finds his father collapsed by the boat only a hundred yards from home, with no idea what he is doing there or where he had been heading, and the family takes him back to a house with a woman he no longer remembers.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Cowen's chosen image for a nostalgic project that collapses before it can even begin — a useful mental model for late-life or late-cycle attempts to relive past success.
insights.quote: only a hundred yards from home, with no idea what he is doing there and where he had been heading
insights.locator: Telemachus finds him in the evening
